LHX.sentence: L3Harris has badly lagged its fellow defense contractors over the past month even though nothing's wrong with the business, which is why it looks unusually cheap here.

ASML.sentence: ASML is quiet and has drifted down a little from its highs, but as the only maker of a crucial chipmaking machine in the world, its story is unchanged.

LIN.sentence: Linde has pulled back more than usual for such a steady company, but industrial gas demand is reliable and they keep raising prices, so this is just a dip rather than a problem.

MSFT.sentence: Microsoft has had a strong run and stretched well ahead of similar companies, so this is more a moment to catch its breath than anything worrying about the AI cloud business.

TMO.sentence: Thermo Fisher looks well-positioned because biotech funding has thawed sharply, and more money flowing to labs eventually means more orders for its equipment.

ENB.sentence: Enbridge dipped a little, but it basically runs a toll road for oil and gas pipelines, so the business is as steady as ever.

NOW.sentence: ServiceNow has fallen a long way from its highs even though it's still growing fast selling workflow-automation and AI tools to big companies and the government, so the drop looks more like fear than a real problem.

GLNCY.sentence: Glencore had a good day and has room to catch up to copper prices, which have been rising and matter a lot to this miner and commodity trader.

RDDT.sentence: Reddit's advertising revenue grew a remarkable 61% last quarter, yet the stock still sits well below its highs on the lingering worry that Google could send it fewer visitors.

KOF.sentence: Coca-Cola FEMSA is calm — the Mexican peso, which is the biggest thing that moves this Latin American Coke bottler, is sitting in a comfortable range.

PBR.A.sentence: Petrobras is paying a very generous dividend and oil prices are cooperating, so the main reason it stays cheap is Brazilian politics rather than anything about the business.

AMKBY.sentence: Maersk slipped a little as shipping rates ease back from their Red Sea–disruption highs, and a wave of new ships arriving over the next couple of years is the thing to watch.

MA.sentence: Mastercard is steady, and it's trading unusually close to Visa's price despite nothing being wrong on its end — people keep tapping their cards more than ever.

ISRG.sentence: The da Vinci surgical robot company has sold off more than its medical-device peers on worries about competition, but there's no actual sign hospitals are using its machines less, so it looks like fear-driven selling.
